brief.headline: The first LME official struck after the weekend US-Iran de-escalation went UP, not down - cash +2.0% to $3,260, the backwardation nearly tripled to +$48 and stock drew a 24th straight session to a century-low 262,650 t - the market's first hard vote that the aluminium tightness is physical, while oil priced the diplomacy with a 5% fall.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. The 03-Aug official settled cash $3,260.00 (+$64.00, +2.00%, highest since early June), 3M $3,212.00 (+1.04%), cash-3M backwardation +$48.00 (from +$17.00, above the late-July peak), LME stock 262,650 t (-1,750 t, 24th consecutive draw, -48.4% year-to-date). Copper and zinc also rose; nickel and lead fell - this was not an indiscriminate metals bid.

WHY IT MATTERS. This was the test both prior compiles set up: a prompt premium that had halved on a demand shock met a supply-side de-escalation headline pointing the same way - and instead of flipping to contango it rebuilt to a new local high while Brent fell about 5%. Oil priced the war premium out; aluminium priced the warehouse. Roughly two days of global consumption in exchange cover means talks about future Gulf supply do not put metal in LME sheds today.

THE COUNTERWEIGHTS. US-Iran talks began Monday afternoon with no published outcome yet; a signed deal plus verified Hormuz transit recovery remains the largest downside catalyst, and supply is already returning without one (outside-China daily output +1.6% m/m in July on Middle East and Iceland restarts). China's downstream remains the soft spot - bar processing fees down nearly 20%, official PMI at 49.2 - though the private 50.9 print and expanding Korea/Taiwan/Vietnam PMIs dispute the demand-collapse read.

WHAT TO WATCH. Today's 13:20-London official - does +$48 hold and does stock break 260,000 t; Alba's Q2 today, the first full-quarter Gulf-disruption P&L, with Century Thursday and Hindalco Friday; published Hormuz transit counts versus about ten vessels pre-weekend; and the Q4 MJP premium talks opening late August off an 11-year-high $395/t Q3 settlement.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: 03-Aug OFFICIAL $3,260.00 versus 31-Jul $3,196.00 = +$64.00 (+2.00%) - the first official of August, the first struck after the weekend US-Iran de-escalation, and the highest official cash since early June. The direction is the story: a 2% RISE on the session the de-escalation was being priced in energy (Brent about -5% on Monday) is the market stating that the aluminium bid is about today's metal, not about the war premium. avg = JULY-2026 monthly mean $3,155.98 (final, published on Westmetall's averages page); June's mean was $3,458.64. SOURCING: taken from Westmetall's German overview page carrying the full 03-Aug board; the English overview was still serving a cached 31-Jul snapshot at this ~06:00-London compile - the documented cache failure mode, this time on the overview itself, caught by cross-checking the two language versions.

kpis.label: LME 3-Month
kpis.note: 03-Aug official $3,212.00 versus 31-Jul $3,179.00 = +$33.00 (+1.04%) - half the prompt's move, so the rally was led from the front of the curve. The 3M took out the $3,205 resistance named in prior compiles; next marked level above is the $3,303 measured 1.0x target, supports at $3,205 (broken resistance) then $3,159.50 (28-Jul swing low, the standing short-term Elliott invalidation). July's 3M mean is final at $3,148.93 against June's $3,438.89.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: BACKWARDATION (cash ABOVE 3M) at +$48.00 on the 03-Aug official, up from +$17.00 on 31-Jul - a near-tripling in one session that exceeds the +$44.00 peak of the late-July widening run. Convention: cash > 3M = backwardation = nearby tightness; cash < 3M = contango. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED THE SAME DIRECTION (both up), and they did it on a session dominated by a bearish supply headline - the de-escalation - which is precisely the test the prior compile said would separate a geopolitical premium from physical scarcity. The spread passed it. The stock series corroborates: a further 1,750 t draw to a century low on the same session.

lme.commentary: THE FIRST POST-DE-ESCALATION OFFICIAL WAS THE TEST, AND THE BULLS WON IT. Cash settled $3,260.00 on 03-Aug, +$64.00 (+2.00%) - the highest official since early June - with 3M up 1.04% at $3,212.00, the backwardation nearly tripling to +$48.00 and stock drawing a 24th straight session to 262,650 t, a fresh century low. Every element of that line moved in the tightness direction on the very session the market was absorbing a cancelled strike, agreed deal perimeters and a 5% fall in Brent. The prior two compiles posed the question explicitly: the spread had compressed 61% on a demand shock (the 49.2 NBS PMI) and then faced a supply-side de-escalation pointing the same way - if it held, the tightness was physical. It did not merely hold; it rebuilt above its late-July peak. The prompt is bidding for metal that exists today, and 262,650 t of exchange cover - about two days of global consumption - is the reason. What would change this read: a verified transit recovery through Hormuz plus the first stock BUILD in 24 sessions; either would put the 28-Jul swing low at $3,159.50 back in play. Until one of those prints, the burden of proof has shifted to the bears.

regional.basis: Q3-2026 SETTLED at $395/t CIF Japan (S&P Global Platts, assessed 06-Jul-2026) - an 11-year high (prior peak Q3-2014 $404/t), +11.9-12.9% q/q versus Q2's $350-353, built from 10 trades at $395/t for a combined minimum 15,500 t/month, July-September loading. QUARTERLY BASIS: this does not re-price daily and no fresher public print exists at this 04-Aug refresh; a dedicated search for Q4-2026 offers, talks coverage or settlement returned nothing public. Talks are expected to open around late August. THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP MOVED AGAINST SELLERS OVER THIS WEEKEND, having moved for them over the previous one. FOR the buyers: Trump cancelled the planned Iran strike on 01-Aug and claims a deal opening the Strait of Hormuz, which attacks the scarcity narrative underneath an 11-year-high premium; Japan and the US confirmed their first JOINT yen intervention since 2011 and the yen has firmed roughly 5% in three sessions to 156.44, mechanically raising the local-currency cost of dollar metal; the official China PMI is in contraction at 49.2; and the LME backwardation has halved to +$17.00. FOR the sellers: exchange stock is at a century low of 264,400 t, EGA had only 89 of 1,262 pots running at 02-Jul, and Alba's Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) have been down since 15-Mar with no public restart date. AL Circle's 24-Jul review notes the CIF Japan premium rose 127% quarter-on-quarter in early 2026 - context for why buyers resisted producer offers of $440-480.

Platts CIF Japan spot P1020/P1020A $370/t over LME cash, assessed 06-Jul-2026. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT - the freshest publicly retrievable mark, now 28 days old at this 04-Aug refresh; it is carried at its assessment date and is NOT a current-session value. No daily move should be inferred. Against the 31-Jul cash official of $3,196.00 an all-in Japanese delivered equivalent computes to roughly $3,566/t, of which the premium is about 10.4%. THE FX LEG IS THE LIVE VARIABLE THIS RUN: USD/JPY is 156.44 on Monday 03-Aug after Japan's Ministry of Finance and the US Treasury confirmed a coordinated yen-buying intervention - the first joint action since 2011 - with Tokyo warning it stands ready to act again. The yen has gained about 5% in three sessions from 163.4 a week earlier. For a Japanese buyer paying in yen, that is a direct reduction in the local-currency cost of the same dollar premium, and it cuts both ways: it improves affordability but it also removes one of the arguments producers used for a higher Q4 number.

European P1020A duty-unpaid in-warehouse Rotterdam, carried at its last public assessment. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT, not a daily mark - no fresher free public print is available at this 04-Aug refresh, so the value is held at its assessment date rather than implied to have moved. The duty-unpaid leg is the cleanest read on genuine European physical tightness because it excludes both the 6% EU import duty and the CBAM cost embedded in duty-paid assessments since January 2026. DISCLOSURE ON WHAT IS AND IS NOT PUBLIC: the duty-PAID Rotterdam assessment does have a post-6-Jul public print - Fastmarkets' 14-Jul-2026 pricing notice carries P1020A duty-paid in-warehouse Rotterdam at $510-540/t - but the duty-UNPAID series (MB-AL-0346) has no publicly retrievable figure dated after early March 2026, so it is NOT updated from the duty-paid read. The regional backdrop turned two-sided over the weekend: European gas fell 4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on the strike cancellation, which improves restart economics at the margin, while the Suez routing that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam remains impaired by the Bab al Mandeb disruption.

6063 extrusion billet premium, in-warehouse duty-paid Rotterdam (Fastmarkets MB-AL-0002 basis), carried at its last public assessment date. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT - not refreshed daily. Billet premiums carry the duty-paid structure plus the conversion spread over P1020, so they move with both metal availability and extruder order books. European extrusion demand remains the soft spot in the regional balance. THE ENERGY LEG IMPROVED THIS RUN: TTF gas fell 4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on Monday 03-Aug after the Iran strike was called off, from EUR 59.07 at the 31-Jul close - the first material downtick in a month that still ran roughly 36-37% higher. Hydro's Slovalco agreement with the Slovak government to resume 75,000 t from Q4-2026 remains the first concrete European restart of the cycle, and cheaper power is exactly the condition that would let others follow. EGA's force majeure on European billet contracts, declared 12-Apr-2026, was still in force at the last public check (20-Jul).

Platts US Midwest transaction premium, carried at its 06-Jul-2026 assessment of roughly $2,380/t (about 108 c/lb) after $2,396/t on 03-Jul; no fresher free public print is retrievable at this 04-Aug refresh, so it is held at its assessment date and no daily move should be inferred. The US premium is overwhelmingly a TARIFF construct rather than a scarcity signal: at the 31-Jul cash of $3,196.00 the 50% Section 232 rate on aluminium articles is $1,598.00/t on its own. The rate was re-verified unchanged this run. A 20-Jul-2026 proclamation additionally allows companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) to import at HALF the applicable rate against expected output; no CBP guidance implementing that measure has been issued yet, and it is the main identified route by which the US premium could compress without any change to the headline tariff.

US Midwest duty-paid P1020A, carried at its last public assessment date - PERIODIC, not a daily mark, and not refreshed this run because no fresher free public print exists. This is the tariff-inflated delivered number and it is the row the tariff decomposition on this board matches against. DECOMPOSITION REFRESHED EVERY RUN: at the 31-Jul cash official of $3,196.00 the 50% Section 232 ad-valorem leg alone is $1,598.00/t, unchanged from the prior compile because the metal price is unchanged; the residual above that is the genuine physical/logistics component. Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs (15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members) run from 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 under Federal Register 2026-11314. Alcoa's Q2-2026 disclosure of roughly $35m of additional Section 232 cost on Canadian metal is the clearest public evidence that the tariff is a real cash cost to cross-border producers as well as a premium inflator.

drivers.text: THE WEEKEND REMOVED THE MARGINAL BUYER OF RISK: Trump cancelled the planned strike on Iran, said the perimeters of a deal are agreed and claimed an immediate and complete opening of the Strait of Hormuz, with talks starting Monday afternoon — Al Jazeera, NPR and Bloomberg all carry the same 02-Aug account: after Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Iran pressed for diplomacy, Trump called off a strike he had planned for the weekend, posted late on 01-Aug that the 'perimeters of a deal' had been reached, and framed the deal as delivering an immediate, complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz. Talks were scheduled to begin Monday afternoon. The market reaction is unambiguous in the energy complex - Brent -4.61% to $83.88 and Dutch TTF -4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on 03-Aug - and every physical aluminium premium on this board has a Gulf-risk component that the same headline attacks. WHAT IS NOT YET SOURCEABLE: no aluminium-specific price assessment or news analysis dated 02-03 Aug has been published on the read-across, so the premium impact stated here is explicitly inference from the energy tape and the June precedent, not an assessed move. The June precedent is on the official record: on the 17-Jun 60-day ceasefire the LME official cash fell from $3,855.00 on 02-Jun to $3,061.50 in early July, -20.6%.
drivers.source: Al Jazeera - Trump cancels Iran strike, says deal perimeters reached (02-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: Physical Gulf supply cannot return on a headline - EGA had 89 of 1,262 pots running at 02-Jul and Alba's Lines 1-3, 19% of a 1,623,000 t/y smelter, have been shut since 15-Mar with no public restart date — This is the strongest argument that premiums do not fully unwind on a diplomatic headline. EGA's own 02-Jul disclosure, carried in SMM's 31-Jul overseas review, gives the first hard public pot count: anode removal complete for all pots, pot cleaning about 90% complete, solidified aluminium cleared from over 20% of pots, and 89 of 1,262 pots back in operation - after the first repaired pot restarted on 26-May. That is roughly 7% of the potline. Alba disclosed on 15-Mar-2026 that it had initiated a controlled shutdown of Reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3, equal to 19% of its 1,623,000 t/y capacity, citing supply and transit disruption affecting the Strait of Hormuz, and on 29-Mar confirmed its facility had been subject to an Iranian attack on 28-Mar with two employees suffering minor injuries. Alba's Q1-2026 results quantified the operational cost: sales volume 312,563 t (-17% y/y) and net finished production 339,734 t (-14% y/y). Restarting a frozen potline is a months-long capital exercise, not a policy decision.
drivers.source: Alba - Q1-2026 results and 15-Mar-2026 Lines 1-3 shutdown disclosure

drivers.text: Gulf war-risk cover at 3-10% of hull value - over $7 million per transit on a $100m vessel versus 0.25% pre-war - reprices on underwriters' cycles, not on headlines, and a tanker was still struck on 01-Aug — AL Circle's 24-Jul Middle East review assembles the public picture: war-risk insurance for Gulf transits stood at roughly 0.25% of hull value before February's escalation, quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes, and by mid-July was quoted at 3-10% - the difference between a $250,000 premium and one exceeding $7 million on a single transit. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. The five GCC smelters produced about 6.16 Mt in 2025 (roughly 8% of world supply) with more than 80% exported; analysts pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of losses through 2026, near 5% of global primary supply. THE TIMING MATTERS: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by a projectile about 20 km north-east of Lima, Oman on 01-Aug - reported as an LNG carrier with Qatari cargo - with a second incident 40 km north-east of Khasab. That was the day of the cancellation, not before it. Insurance is a lagging, contractual cost; it will not fall on the announcement of talks.
drivers.source: AL Circle - 2026 Middle East aluminium outlook: 5% of global supply, USD 7 million insurance and the Hormuz effect (24-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: US Section 232 at 50% is $1,598.00/t of the US duty-paid premium at the 31-Jul cash - re-verified unchanged this run, and the tariff leg is flat because the metal price is flat — Aluminium articles made entirely or almost entirely of aluminium pay 50% ad valorem on full customs value; derivative aluminium content pays 25%. The structure originates in the April-2026 proclamation and was further adjusted by the 01-Jun-2026 proclamation (Federal Register 2026-11314, effective 08-Jun-2026), whose 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 window applies to the Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs - 15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members. A 20-Jul-2026 proclamation additionally lets companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) import at half the applicable rate against expected output; no CBP guidance has been issued yet. MECHANICS: at the 31-Jul cash of $3,196.00 the 50% leg computes to $1,598.00/t exactly, unchanged from the prior compile because no new official has printed. This is the reason the US premium is not a clean scarcity signal and must not be read alongside MJP or EDU as if it were.
drivers.source: Federal Register 2026-11314 - Adjusting imports of aluminum into the United States (effective 08-Jun-2026); 20-Jul-2026 smelter-investment proclamation

Supply context both ways: EGA's Al Taweelah refinery is ramping back after a three-and-a-half-month outage but does not expect full alumina capability until year-end (2.4 Mt in 2025, 46% of company feedstock needs), while Rio Tinto's Yarwun will be cut 40% from October 2026 on tailings constraints.

prices.label: Bauxite (Guinea, CIF China)
prices.note: REFRESHED THIS RUN: SMM's 31-Jul alumina cost analysis states Guinea bauxite at $70-75/mt, against just over $60/mt in December 2025 - a fresher and better-dated public reference than the ~$70/mt spot print of 05-Jun previously carried, and it is the bauxite input SMM uses to derive the roughly 2,530 yuan/mt Chinese alumina industry cost floor. SMM's 02-Aug inventory note adds that bauxite stocks at ten Chinese ports fell 730,000 mt week-on-week as at 31-Jul, the first materially tighter port read of the cycle. Set against that, oversupply remains structural: Guinea shipped a RECORD 114.8 Mt in H1-2026, +15% y/y, and China's alumina imports ran +749% y/y to 2.28 Mt in H1 with 91.7% of it Australian. A 2026 Guinea export cap near 150 Mt has been considered but NOT implemented. SMM's granular live assessment remains paywalled.

prices.note: CNY 2,090/t delivered, 50% ion-membrane liquid on a 100% NaOH basis, July purchase price held flat month-on-month at Shanxi alumina plants (SMM, 02-Jul-2026) - 32 days old at this refresh; the August contract cycle has not yet produced a public print and is the next scheduled update for this line. This Chinese contract line is the dated, sourceable substitute.

prices.note: $163/MT China monthly average for June 2026, against $156/MT in Q1-2026 (IMARC quicklime pricing report); July's monthly average has no public print yet. No alumina-refinery-grade lime assessment is published publicly and there is no liquid global index - the causticisation reagent is largely regional and contract-priced, so this generic average is indicative only.

notes: Alumina is roughly 1.92 t per tonne of aluminium and typically 30-40% of smelter cash cost, so it is the single largest determinant of where the industry cost curve sits and therefore of how far the metal price can fall before supply responds. That question is unusually live this run: with the weekend de-escalation pulling the metal price down, a falling alumina cost removes the floor that would otherwise force curtailment.

THE PRECISE CURRENT SMM CHINA INDEX LEVEL IS NOT PUBLISHED HERE because it sits behind SMM's paywall. The last free print of 2,730.17 yuan/mt is carried at 16-Jul-2026, and the date was deliberately NOT upgraded this run: a re-check returned the identical value against a later page date, so the index could not be confirmed as having advanced. The fresher, better-dated China mark quoted alongside it is the SHFE most-traded alumina close of 2,621 yuan/mt on 31-Jul. Where only a direction is publicly sourceable, only the direction is published.

THE MARKS ON THIS TABLE ARE OF DIFFERENT VINTAGES AND EACH ROW STATES ITS OWN. The CME futures line is the freshest and was REFRESHED THIS RUN to $333.34/t; SMM's FOB Western Australia assessment is carried at 09-Jul; the Platts FOB Australia mark at 26-Jun is stale at 38 days. Ex-China supply is two-sided: EGA's Al Taweelah refinery is ramping back after a three-and-a-half-month outage but does not expect full alumina capability until year-end (2.4 Mt in 2025, 46% of company feedstock needs), while Rio Tinto's Yarwun will be cut 40% from October 2026 on tailings constraints.

COMMERCIAL LOGIC OF A FALLING COST FLOOR: cheap alumina is a principal reason the July earnings season was uniformly strong across the producer set - Alcoa's Aluminum segment posted record EBITDA at a 32.3% margin and Hydro beat on adjusted EBITDA. It is also why a falling metal price does not immediately translate into supply discipline. Chinese operating capacity is 45.31 Mt/y against a 45 Mt ceiling with H1 output of 22.34 Mt (+2.24% y/y); with alumina near its cost floor and energy now falling too, there is no cost-side mechanism forcing that capacity out. Watch the SHFE alumina contract's test of 2,600 yuan/mt as the marker.

items.note: CNY 5,683/t cash (5,707 acceptance) - July 2026 procurement benchmark at a major Shandong smelter, +CNY 30/t month-on-month, published 17-18 Jul-2026. logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk insurance for Gulf transits stood at roughly 0.25% of hull value before February's escalation, quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes, and by mid-July was quoted at 3-10% - the difference between a $250,000 premium and one exceeding $7 million on a single $100m-hull transit. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. THIS IS THE SLOWEST-MOVING PART OF THE DELIVERED-COST STACK AND IT WILL NOT FALL ON AN ANNOUNCEMENT. Underwriters reprice on their own cycles against realised loss experience, and the most recent realised loss is the 01-Aug tanker strike near Lima, Oman - the same day as the cancellation. Even on a signed agreement, the insurance wedge is likely to persist for months, which puts a floor under Gulf-origin delivered costs independent of the LME price.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, 13:20 London - the follow-through test. Three reads: (1) does the rebuilt +$48.00 backwardation hold, extend or give back; (2) does the 3M consolidate above the broken $3,205 level; (3) does the stock draw extend a 25th session toward the 260,000 t threshold, now only 2,650 t away.

ALBA (Aluminium Bahrain) Q2 and H1-2026 results, per its published financial calendar - the most direct Gulf-disruption read available: first full-quarter producer P&L with Reduction Lines 1-3 (about 19% of 1,623,000 t/y) offline since 15-Mar. Q1's template was volume down, profit up on the higher LME; watch restart guidance on Lines 1-3 and the first Aluminium Dunkerque consolidation. Not yet published at this compile.

HORMUZ AND BAB AL MANDEB TRANSIT COUNTS - the observable that decides whether Monday's diplomacy is real. Hormuz ran about ten commodity vessels on 31-Jul against more than 100 pre-war. A recovery toward pre-war levels is the single most bearish development possible for the premium complex; continued single-digit transits would mean the announcement changed nothing physical.

WHETHER LME STOCK BREAKS 260,000 t - the draw has run 24 consecutive published sessions to 262,650 t, -48.4% year-to-date. At the recent draw rate the threshold breaks within two sessions. The first BUILD would be far more significant than any further draw: it would mean metal returning to warehouse as the risk premium unwinds.

Century Aluminum Q2-2026 results (after US close, confirmed by the company) - the purest US and Section-232 read in the peer set, and the cleanest test of how much of the roughly $2,380/t US Midwest premium is converting into margin with Mt. Holly back at full capacity for the first time since 2015.

Hindalco Q1 FY27 results - management has guided to roughly 5% higher aluminium costs, so the read is whether Indian integrated economics hold as the risk premium trades off. India is the swing consumer the bull case relies on outside China.

SMM weekly China aluminium ingot and billet social inventory - the direct test of whether the sub-1 Mt destocking (953,000 t at 30-Jul, -35% from the early-May high) continues into the seasonal off-peak, with bar processing fees already down nearly 20% and extruder rates falling.

SMM alumina index and the SHFE alumina contract's test of 2,600 yuan/mt - flagged explicitly by SMM, with the most-traded contract near 2,621 against an industry cost floor near 2,530 on Guinea bauxite at $70-75/mt. A break below 2,600 removes what is left of the cost-push argument.

Q4-2026 MJP CIF Japan premium negotiations expected to open - Q3 settled at an 11-year high of $395/t on 06-Jul. The backdrop has turned mixed: de-escalation attacks the scarcity case and the yen is roughly 5% firmer after joint intervention, but the LME backwardation has REBUILT to +$48.00 and exchange stock is at a century low - sellers enter with more evidence than they had a week ago.
China August PMIs and industrial output - whether July's split (private RatingDog 50.9 versus official NBS 49.2) resolves upward or downward - then the 15-16 September FOMC with dots.

risks.text: THE DIPLOMATIC BREAKTHROUGH IS STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE RISK ON THE BOARD - talks began Monday afternoon after Trump cancelled the planned strike, said deal perimeters were agreed and called for an immediate and complete reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The June precedent stands on the official record: on the 17-Jun ceasefire the official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6%. Monday's 2% RISE does not retire this risk - it shows the market will not pre-pay the de-escalation, which makes the repricing on a SIGNED, verified deal with observable transit recovery potentially sharper, not gentler. No outcome from Monday's session had been published at this compile.

THE PROMPT PREMIUM PASSED ITS SECOND TEST AND THE FLIP RISK HAS RECEDED - the cash-3M backwardation, having compressed from +$44.00 to +$17.00 on the 49.2 NBS PMI demand shock, faced the weekend supply-side de-escalation and instead of flipping to contango REBUILT to +$48.00, a new local high, on the same session the flat price rose 2%. The residual version of this risk is now event-conditional rather than trend-driven: a verified transit recovery plus the first stock build in 24 sessions would still unwind the spread quickly, and the June episode showed how fast that repricing runs.

SUPPLY IS RETURNING WITHOUT A DEAL AND WOULD ACCELERATE WITH ONE - outside-China daily-average output rose 1.6% month-on-month in July on Middle East and Iceland restarts, with Slovalco +75 kt from Q4-26, Marston +75 kt, Alcoa 636 kt (+5% q/q) and Balco 168 kt (+17% y/y). Chinese operating capacity is 45.31 Mt/y against a 45 Mt cap with H1 output 22.34 Mt (+2.24% y/y), and an industry margin of 6,999 yuan/mt (+56.8% y/y) removes any incentive for restraint. Cheaper energy after the de-escalation makes idled European capacity more likely to return.

THE COST FLOOR IS FALLING WITH THE PRICE - Brent -4.61% to $83.88 and TTF -4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh cut petroleum-coke, anode and power costs; Chinese alumina at 2,621 yuan/mt on the SHFE sits only about 3.6% above SMM's stated 2,530 yuan/mt industry cost floor, with SMM warning it may break 2,600 in August against port inventory at a cycle-high 940,000 mt. Falling input costs remove the cost-push argument for defending the metal price, though they also protect smelter margins on the way down.

CHINESE DOWNSTREAM DEMAND IS THE WEAK LINK EVEN AS THE SURVEYS IMPROVE - aluminium bar processing fees have slumped nearly 20% as orders dry up in the seasonal off-peak, extruder operating rates are falling, and SMM attributes the ingot destocking to supply contraction and a rising liquid-aluminium share (78.3%, forecast 78.5% in August) rather than to demand pull. The official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 with non-manufacturing at 49.0.

A FIRMER YEN AFTER JOINT US-JAPAN INTERVENTION COMPLICATES THE Q4 PREMIUM - the first coordinated yen-buying action since 2011 has taken USD/JPY to 156.44, roughly 5% firmer in three sessions from 163.4, with Tokyo warning it will act again. It cuts both ways: cheaper dollar metal in local currency improves Japanese affordability, but it also removes an argument producers were using to justify a higher Q4-2026 CIF Japan premium off an 11-year-high $395/t base, and MJP negotiations open around late August.

EXTERNAL DEMAND IS OUTPERFORMING THE OFFICIAL CHINA SURVEY - the private RatingDog July manufacturing PMI printed 50.9, in expansion, against NBS 49.2, with new orders up a 14th month and foreign sales rising for the first time in three. Korea 53.1, Taiwan 55.1 and Vietnam 52.9 all expanded with export orders improving. This is a risk to the BEARISH case: the demand collapse the 49.2 print implied is not confirmed by any other Asian survey.

Tightening risk is DEFERRED, NOT REMOVED - the Fed held 9-3 with three dissents FOR a hike on 29-Jul and the Bank of England 6-3 on 30-Jul, with the US 10-year at 4.74%. June US core PCE at +0.1% m/m and 3.3% y/y leans dovish, and a sustained fall in oil and gas after the de-escalation would take the energy impulse out of the second-half inflation path - which on balance now points AWAY from a hike and is dollar-negative at the margin. The 15-16 September FOMC with dots is the decision point.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. China alone ran a 322 kt deficit in June, and exchange inventory at a fresh century low leaves no absorption capacity

Consensus expects surpluses as Gulf output recovers and Indonesia ramps; Concord Resources warns the market may be 'too complacent about supply risks' in the meantime. Rio Tinto's 40% Yarwun alumina cut from October 2026 trims one input to that surplus
